notes: Hand-verified against the scenario's own arithmetic before comparing to reference-model output. Every month: gross pay 5000.00; withheld from the employee: federal 800.00, state 200.00, FICA 382.50 (totaling 1382.50); net pay to the employee 5000.00 − 1382.50 = 3617.50, paid immediately. Employer also owes a matching FICA share of 382.50 as payroll_tax_expense, added to the same fica_payable account (now holding 765.00 — both shares). Total monthly payable accrual: 800.00 + 200.00 + 765.00 = 1765.00, remitted in cash the following month (the same one-month accrual/payment lag as ACCR-001).
Every month has identical income-statement activity: service_revenue 8000.00, salaries_expense 5000.00, payroll_tax_expense 382.50, net income 2617.50.

2026-01 (January, no prior-month liability to remit yet): cash = 10000.00 (opening) + 8000.00 (revenue) − 3617.50 (net pay) = 14382.50 (no remittance this month). Liabilities at month end: federal 800.00, state 200.00, fica 765.00 (January's own accrual, unremitted until February). Balance sheet: assets 14382.50 = liabilities 1765.00 + equity (owner_equity 10000.00 + current_period_earnings 2617.50) 12617.50 — 1765.00 + 12617.50 = 14382.50. Cash flow: net_income 2617.50 + owner_equity +10000.00 (the opening contribution) + federal +800.00 + state +200.00 + fica +765.00 = 14382.50, matching ending_cash 14382.50 − beginning_cash 0.00.

2026-06 (June, standalone month, steady state — a prior month's liability is remitted and a new one accrues, netting to zero liability change): cash change = 8000.00 (revenue) − 3617.50 (net pay) − 1765.00 (May's liability, remitted) = 2617.50 — equal to net income exactly, since the liability accounts' net delta for the month is 0.00 (1765.00 remitted, 1765.00 newly accrued). current_period_earnings (January–June, no closing yet) = 6 × 2617.50 = 15705.00.

2026-12 (December, standalone month, after the single fiscal-year closing): same steady-state activity as June (net income 2617.50, cash change 2617.50). December's own accrual (1765.00) remains unremitted at year end — it would be paid in January 2027, outside this scenario's window — so the balance sheet still shows liabilities of 1765.00 (same composition as every other month-end). retained_earnings = 31410.00 (the full year's net income, swept in by the closing).

2026 (full fiscal year): revenue 12×8000.00 = 96000.00; salaries_expense 12×5000.00 = 60000.00; payroll_tax_expense 12×382.50 = 4590.00; net income 31410.00.
